elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay liquidated damages or other liquidated amounts.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) requires the Company to pay an “early-termination fee” and expressly characterizes it as a “liquidated amount payable by the Company.”

elements.element: Customer has no obligation to pay penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not impose or authorize any separate penalty payable by the Company.

elements.element: The permitted liquidated payment is an early-termination fee triggered by Customer’s termination of the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The payment applies “[i]n the event the Company terminates this Agreement” and is expressly designated an “early-termination fee.”

elements.element: The early-termination fee does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: The fee is fixed at “the fees payable under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date,” so it cannot exceed the stated three-month measure.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) expressly states that the fee “shall be the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company under this Agreement.”

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because it retains a liquidated payment obligation. It achieves the fallback by recasting the payment as an early-termination fee measured by three months of Section 3.1 fees and making that fee the sole liquidated amount payable by the Company. The changes are confined to the payment type, amount, and exclusivity language; the existing no-payment floor and installment schedule remain intact. Drafting quality is reduced slightly by the pre-existing sentence fragment beginning “Payment is determined,” but it does not defeat the fallback.
